candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated HTTP client. The print request body is fully client-controlled JSON; its `attributes` are parsed against the template's declared attributes (Values.populateFromAttributes / MapfishParser). A map attribute's `layers` array is parsed by GenericMapAttribute.parseLayers/parseSingleLayer (GenericMapAttribute.java:437-500), and for a layer of type `image` the attacker supplies `baseURL` (ImageLayer.ImageParam.baseURL, ImageLayer.java:192), which ImageLayer passes verbatim to `new URI(...)` and to the HTTP request factory (ImageLayer.java:82-94). Other request-controlled URI strings reach the same loader (e.g. layer `style` references via ParserPluginUtils.loadStyleAsURI, table image URLs via HttpImageResolver, `!northArrow` `graphic`).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The sibling branches in resolveChildFile and resolveFileAssumingPathIsFile do call FileUtils.assertIsSubDirectory (lines 149/157/167/192), and the 2-arg loadFile only reads what resolveChildFile returns, so this is a single missing check rather than a documented exception. Explicit `file:` URIs, `file://host/...`, and absolute paths are rejected by the asserts; java.io.File(parent,child) concatenates absolute children on Unix, so only `../`-style relative traversal bypasses the directory restriction. `!geojson`, `!gml` and `!geotiff` layer URLs are additionally screened by FileUtils.testForLegalFileUrl, and the 1-arg ConfigFileLoaderManager.loadFile(URI) (which the ClasspathConfigFileLoader would read for any existing `file:` URI) is only invoked with administrator-configured config files, so those are not the primary vector. The GenericMapAttribute layer-loop and Values population confirm attacker control of layer params; ImageIO rejects non-image content, which bounds direct exfiltration to images (Jobs' error strings are derived from the unwrapped root cause, which usually drops content-bearing wrapper messages such as FeaturesParser's 'Invalid geoJSON: <data>').
candidates.impact: Arbitrary local file read with the privileges of the servlet/JVM user, bypassing the documented guarantee that file URLs/relative paths must resolve inside the configuration directory. Full disclosure of any decodable image file on the server through the generated report (e.g. other apps' images, user-uploaded content); existence/type oracle and server-side read of all other readable files (configuration/secret files, /etc/passwd, etc.), whose content may additionally surface in debug logs or in downstream parsers. The scheme-less URI also bypasses !restrictUris/!mapUri matcher logic.
candidates.prerequisites: A deployed print app/template that declares a map attribute (standard) and permits a layer type that forwards a scheme-less URI, or any other template flow that calls Configuration.loadFile with an attacker-influenced path string. The default servlet security config permits all URLs unauthenticated (mapfish-spring-security.xml:20-23), and app/attribute names are discoverable via /apps.json and /capabilities.json. The target file must exist relative to the configuration directory (`.getDirectory()` is in the repository?); the loader's other branches block `file:` URIs and absolute paths via FileUtils.assertIsSubDirectory.
candidates.root_cause: AbstractFileConfigFileLoader.resolveFileAssumingPathIsFile() (core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/fileloader/AbstractFileConfigFileLoader.java:183-199) handles a non-URI sub-resource by doing `new File(configFile.getParentFile(), pathToSubResource)` and returning it whenever it exists (lines 185-188), WITHOUT calling FileUtils.assertIsSubDirectory(). All sibling resolution branches enforce containment (lines 149, 157, 167, 192), and Configuration.loadFile()/ConfigFileLoaderPlugin javadoc explicitly promise that only files inside the configuration (or working) directory can be loaded. Because `pathToSubResource` is attacker-influenced and `File(parent, child)` simply concatenates on Unix, a value containing `../` segments (e.g. `../../../../../etc/passwd`) escapes the configuration directory and is read by AbstractFileConfigFileLoader.loadFile(URI,String) (lines 114-121).
candidates.title: Path traversal in AbstractFileConfigFileLoader allows arbitrary local file read from print requests
candidates.trace: 1) POST /print/{app}/report.pdf (or /print/report.pdf with `app` in the JSON) -> MapPrinterServlet.createReport (MapPrinterServlet.java:399-428) -> job submitted (createAndSubmitPrintJob, lines 978-1023). 2) PrintJob runs MapPrinter.print -> AbstractJasperReportOutputFormat.getJasperPrint -> Values -> CreateMapProcessor, which passes the per-template `clientHttpRequestFactoryProvider.get()` to the layers (CreateMapProcessor.java:235-239). 3) ImageLayer.loadImage does `new URI(layerParam.getBaseUrl())` and `requestFactory.createRequest(commonUri, HttpMethod.GET)` (ImageLayer.java:82-94) with baseURL = `../../../../../../etc/passwd`. 4) If any http processor wraps the factory, AbstractMfClientHttpRequestFactoryWrapper.createRequest (line 51) passes the request through because `uri.getScheme() == null`, so `!restrictUris` matchers do not apply. 5) ConfigFileResolvingHttpRequestFactory.ConfigFileResolvingRequest.executeInternal (lines 112-124) calls `configuration.loadFile(uriString)` before any real HTTP request. 6) Configuration.loadFile(String) -> ConfigFileLoaderManager.loadFile(configUri, path) -> FileConfigFileLoader/AbstractFileConfigFileLoader.isAccessible(URI,String) (lines 104-112) -> resolveChildFile (lines 133-181) -> resolveFileAssumingPathIsFile (lines 183-199): `new File(configFile.getParentFile(), '../../../../../../etc/passwd')` exists and is returned with no containment assert, so isAccessible() is true and loadFile(URI,String) (lines 114-121) returns Files.readAllBytes() of the traversed file. 7) The bytes are handed back to ImageLayer.fetchImage (ImageLayer.java:153-218); decodable images are rendered into the report, which the attacker retrieves via GET /report/{ref} (MapPrinterServlet.java:914-937). For non-image files ImageIO returns null and the job either succeeds with an error tile (failOnError=false) or fails - a file existence/readability oracle.
candidates.unverified: No runtime/test execution was performed: the traversal and the image-based exfiltration were established by source tracing only. Whether a particular deployed template exposes a suitable attribute/layer was not verified. Full disclosure of non-image (text) files is not demonstrated end-to-end; the concrete evidence there is unauthorized server-side read plus an existence oracle. The upstream fix history could not be inspected to confirm this exact check was the patched root cause.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); CWE-73 External Control of File Name or Path

coverage_summary: Scope reported by get_source_scope: 442 model-visible files, no over-5MiB, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions; binary-like files are refused/skipped. I reviewed the core Java sources of the servlet/login boundary (MapPrinterServlet, BaseMapServlet, security/app factory, file loaders), the request/attribute/parser path (Values, MapfishParser, GenericMapAttribute, MapAttribute, layer params), the HTTP layer (ConfigFileResolvingHttpRequestFactory, MfClientHttpRequestFactoryImpl, AbstractMfClientHttpRequestFactoryWrapper, URI matchers, processors), map/vector/raster layer readers (image, WMS/WMTS/OSM, GeoJSON/GML/GeoTIFF, NorthArrowGraphic, CachingUrihandler), Jasper/table/legend/data-source processors, job queue/storage/servlet registry classes, config classes (Configuration, S3ReportStorage, SmtpConfig, WorkingDirectories, PDFConfig), webapp/Spring resources (web.xml, mapfish-spring-*.xml, properties) and the CLI. Not deeply reviewed: the 2 MB example GeoJSON/jMeter payloads, docs assets/Groovy generators, and third-party library internals; no tests are present in the snapshot. The strongest issue traced across files is the missing directory-containment check in the configuration file loader.
limitations: Static review only; no code was executed, built, or tested, and no request was sent to any server. The traversal and exfiltration chain is inferred from source.
The snapshot contains no tests, so intended loader behavior could only be compared against in-code javadoc/assert patterns, not against existing test expectations.

Whether a given deployment exposes a template/attribute that reaches the loader with attacker-controlled path strings depends on configuration; the default security config permits unauthenticated requests but app templates are administrator-defined.

Direct content disclosure is demonstrated for decodable image files only; for other file types the evidence supports unauthorized read plus an existence/type oracle and possible debug-log exposure, not guaranteed client-side exfiltration.
Upstream fix history / advisories could not be consulted (no network, no git history in scope), so the exact patched root cause is not confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractMfClientHttpRequestFactoryWrapper.createRequest passes scheme-less and 'file' URIs through without consulting the URI matchers (line 51), which lets requests bypass !restrictUris rules.
rejected_leads.reason: Real matcher bypass, but by itself 'file:' URIs are still containment-checked inside the loader (asserts at AbstractFileConfigFileLoader.java:149/157/167), so it enables the traversal candidate rather than being an independent disclosure; kept as supporting condition in the main finding.

rejected_leads.lead: MfClientHttpRequestFactoryImpl builds its HttpClient with HttpClients.custom() and no custom RedirectStrategy, so Apache HttpClient default redirect-following could bypass !restrictUris by redirecting an allowed URL to an internal address (SSRF).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible but configuration-dependent and not verifiable from this snapshot without running the client; no source-level assertion that redirects are unchecked besides the absent custom strategy. Rejected in favour of the file-loader defect with direct source evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: ServletMapPrinterFactory.checkForAddedApp (lines 222-250) builds a URI from the attacker-supplied app id after replacing ':' with '/', allowing '..' traversal to register a config.yaml outside appsRootDirectory.
rejected_leads.reason: Only works when appsRootDirectory is configured in URI form; it can only load a directory that already contains config.yaml and exposes that app's capabilities rather than returning file contents; weaker and more deployment-specific than the loader traversal.

rejected_leads.lead: RequestSizeFilter compares request.getContentLength() against the limit (RequestSizeFilter.java:38), which is -1 for chunked requests, so the 1 MB limit can be bypassed (DoS).
rejected_leads.reason: Generic body-size-limit bypass; impact is availability only and depends on the container's chunked handling. Lower severity than the file read.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected JSONP callback is written unescaped (appendJsonpCallback, MapPrinterServlet.java:1089-1096) on /status, /apps.json and /capabilities.json.
rejected_leads.reason: Response is application/javascript; no demonstrable cross-origin XSS against the print server origin from a navigable URL, and the callback is not used for secrets. Not compelling enough.

rejected_leads.lead: XML parsing without secure processing: SLDParserPlugin.tryLoadSLD DocumentBuilderFactory (lines 95-99), AbstractJasperReportOutputFormat.parseXML (lines 320-326) and NorthArrowGraphic.parseSvg via Batik SAXSVGDocumentFactory (lines 316-322).
rejected_leads.reason: XXE could be reachable through attacker-supplied style/SVG content, but the parsed entity data is not clearly returned to the client and the effective parser configuration (Batik/JDK defaults, xercesImpl excluded from the build) could not be confirmed statically. Unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: MapPrinterServlet.checkReferer defaults a missing Referer header to 'http://localhost/' (lines 1025-1043), so the allowed-referers restriction can be bypassed by not sending Referer when a localhost matcher is configured.
rejected_leads.reason: Empty-Referer handling is plausibly intentional (non-browser clients); the feature is disabled when allowedReferers is null and is a secondary abuse control, not an authentication boundary.

rejected_leads.lead: ClasspathConfigFileLoader.isAccessible(URI) has no scheme check and loadResources() returns file-system URLs for 'file:' URIs.
rejected_leads.reason: The 1-arg ConfigFileLoaderManager.loadFile(URI) path that would read such resources is only called with administrator-configured configuration files, not with attacker input.

summary: MapFish Print 3.22.0: the configuration file loader returns files resolved relative to the configuration directory without any containment check, so an unauthenticated print request that supplies a scheme-less relative URI (e.g. an `!image` layer `baseURL` such as `../../../../etc/passwd`) is read off the server filesystem. The same loader branches that handle absolute paths and `file:`/scheme URIs do call FileUtils.assertIsSubDirectory, and the method's own javadoc states files outside the configuration directory must not be reachable, so the missing check is an asymmetry/oversight rather than intended behavior. Confidence in the code defect is high; confidence in end-to-end disclosure is medium because the cleanest delivery path (`!image` layer) only returns fully decoded images to the client, while other files are read into memory and act only as an existence/type oracle (content may also appear in debug logs or be parsed by style/SVG consumers).
